{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_732b2df89a12494d90c31aa0","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Building AgentScribe Plugins\n2\t\n3\tThis guide explains how to create a scraper plugin for AgentScribe. A plugin teaches AgentScribe how to find, read, and normalize conversation logs from a specific coding agent.\n4\t\n5\t## What a Plugin Is\n6\t\n7\tA plugin is a single TOML file that declares:\n8\t\n9\t1. **Where** to find log files on disk\n10\t2. **What format** the logs are in\n11\t3. **How to detect session boundaries** within the logs\n12\t4. **How to map fields** from the agent's native format to AgentScribe's canonical schema\n13\t\n14\tNo code is required. If your agent writes logs in a supported format (JSONL, Markdown, JSON tree, SQLite), you only need a TOML file.\n15\t\n16\t---\n17\t\n18\t## Quick Start\n19\t\n20\tCreate a file at `~/.agentscribe/plugins/<agent-name>.toml`:\n21\t\n22\t```toml\n23\t[plugin]\n24\tname = \"my-agent\"\n25\tversion = \"1.0\"\n26\t\n27\t[source]\n28\tpaths = [\"~/.my-agent/history/*.jsonl\"]\n29\tformat = \"jsonl\"\n30\t\n31\t[source.session_detection]\n32\tmethod = \"one-file-per-session\"\n33\tsession_id_from = \"filename\"\n34\t\n35\t[parser]\n36\ttimestamp = \"timestamp\"\n37\trole = \"role\"\n38\tcontent = \"content\"\n39\t\n40\t[parser.static]\n41\tsource_agent = \"my-agent\"\n42\t```\n43\t\n44\tValidate it:\n45\t\n46\t```bash\n47\tagentscribe plugins validate ~/.agentscribe/plugins/my-agent.toml\n48\t```\n49\t\n50\tTest a scrape:\n51\t\n52\t```bash\n53\tagentscribe scrape --plugin my-agent --dry-run\n54\t```\n55\t\n56\t---\n57\t\n58\t## Plugin Specification\n59\t\n60\t### `[plugin]` — Identity\n61\t\n62\t| Field     | Required | Description                              |\n63\t|-----------|----------|------------------------------------------|\n64\t| `name`    | yes      | Unique identifier for this agent type. Used in session IDs, CLI filters, and output directory names. Must be lowercase, alphanumeric, and hyphens only. |\n65\t| `version` | yes      | Plugin definition version. Increment when you change the field mapping or source paths. AgentScribe uses this to detect when re-scraping is needed. |\n66\t\n67\t### `[source]` — Where to Find Logs\n68\t\n69\t| Field     | Required | Description                              |\n70\t|-----------|----------|------------------------------------------|\n71\t| `paths`   | yes      | Array of glob patterns pointing to log files. Supports `~` (home dir), `$ENV_VAR` expansion, and standard glob syntax (`*`, `**`, `?`). |\n72\t| `exclude` | no       | Array of glob patterns to exclude from matches. Evaluated after `paths`. |\n73\t| `format`  | yes      | Log file format. One of: `jsonl`, `markdown`, `json-tree`, `sqlite`. See [Format Reference](#format-reference) below. |\n74\t\n75\t**Path examples:**\n76\t```toml\n77\t# Single known location\n78\tpaths = [\"~/.my-agent/conversations/*.jsonl\"]\n79\t\n80\t# Multiple search roots for project-local files\n81\tpaths = [\"~/projects/*/.my-agent.log\", \"~/repos/*/.my-agent.log\"]\n82\t\n83\t# Recursive search\n84\tpaths = [\"~/.my-agent/**/session-*.json\"]\n85\t\n86\t# Environment variable expansion\n87\tpaths = [\"$MY_AGENT_DATA_DIR/logs/*.jsonl\"]\n88\t```\n89\t\n90\t### `[source.envelope]` — Envelope Unwrapping (Optional)\n91\t\n92\tFor JSONL sources where each line is wrapped in an envelope structure (e.g., `{timestamp, type, payload}`), configure envelope unwrapping to extract the actual event payload.\n93\t\n94\t```toml\n95\t[source.envelope]\n96\tpayload_field = \"data\"     # Field containing the event payload object\n97\ttype_field = \"type\"        # Field containing the event type for routing\n98\t\n99\t[source.envelope.type_routing]\n100\t\"message\" = \"event\"       # Parse as regular event\n101\t\"metadata\" = \"meta\"        # Session metadata (not an event)\n102\t\"heartbeat\" = \"skip\"      # Skip this type entirely\n103\t```\n104\t\n105\t**Routing actions:**\n106\t- `event` - Extract the payload and parse it as a regular event using `[parser]` field mappings\n107\t- `meta` - Session-level metadata (for future use; currently skipped)\n108\t- `skip` - Ignore this line entirely\n109\t\n110\t**Envelope-level field access:**\n111\tUse the `^` prefix in field mappings to access fields from the envelope wrapper instead of the payload:\n112\t\n113\t```toml\n114\t[parser]\n115\ttimestamp = \"^timestamp\"  # From envelope: {\"timestamp\": \"...\", \"type\": \"...\", \"data\": {...}}\n116\trole = \"role\"             # From payload: {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"...\"}\n117\tcontent = \"content\"\n118\t```\n119\t\n120\t**Unknown types:** Any type value not in `type_routing` defaults to `skip` with a warning.\n121\t\n122\t**Example (Codex rollouts):**\n123\t```json\n124\t{\"timestamp\": \"2026-03-16T12:00:00Z\", \"type\": \"message\", \"data\": {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Fix the bug\"}}\n125\t{\"timestamp\": \"2026-03-16T12:00:05Z\", \"type\": \"metadata\", \"data\": {\"model\": \"gpt-4\"}}\n126\t{\"timestamp\": \"2026-03-16T12:00:10Z\", \"type\": \"heartbeat\", \"data\": {\"status\": \"ok\"}}\n127\t```\n128\t\n129\t```toml\n130\t[source.envelope]\n131\tpayload_field = \"data\"\n132\ttype_field = \"type\"\n133\t\n134\t[source.envelope.type_routing]\n135\t\"message\" = \"event\"\n136\t\"metadata\" = \"meta\"\n137\t\"heartbeat\" = \"skip\"\n138\t\n139\t[parser]\n140\ttimestamp = \"^timestamp\"\n141\trole = \"role\"\n142\tcontent = \"content\"\n143\t```\n144\t\n145\t### `[source.session_detection]` — Session Boundaries\n146\t\n147\tAgents store sessions differently. Some create one file per session. Others append to a single continuous file. This section tells AgentScribe how to split logs into discrete sessions.\n148\t\n149\t| Field              | Required | Description                              |\n150\t|--------------------|----------|------------------------------------------|\n151\t| `method`           | yes      | Detection strategy. One of: `one-file-per-session`, `timestamp-gap`, `delimiter`. |\n152\t| `session_id_from`  | depends  | Where to extract the session ID. Required for `one-file-per-session`. |\n153\t| `gap_threshold`    | depends  | Time gap that signals a new session. Required for `timestamp-gap`. Format: `\"30m\"`, `\"2h\"`, `\"1d\"`. |\n154\t| `delimiter_pattern`| depends  | Regex pattern that marks session boundaries. Required for `delimiter`. |\n155\t\n156\t**Method: `one-file-per-session`**\n157\t\n158\tEach log file is one session. Most agents work this way.\n159\t\n160\t```toml\n161\t[source.session_detection]\n162\tmethod = \"one-file-per-session\"\n163\tsession_id_from = \"filename\"     # Use the filename (minus extension) as session ID\n164\t# OR\n165\tsession_id_from = \"field:sessionId\"  # Extract from a JSON field in the first line\n166\t```\n167\t\n168\t**Method: `timestamp-gap`**\n169\t\n170\tFor agents that append to a single file (e.g., Aider). A new session starts when the gap between consecutive entries exceeds the threshold.\n171\t\n172\t```toml\n173\t[source.session_detection]\n174\tmethod = \"timestamp-gap\"\n175\tgap_threshold = \"30m\"\n176\t```\n177\t\n178\tNote: requires the `timestamp` field mapping in `[parser]` to work. If the source format has no timestamps, use `delimiter` instead.\n179\t\n180\t**Method: `delimiter`**\n181\t\n182\tSplit on a pattern in the log content. Useful for agents that write explicit session markers.\n183\t\n184\t```toml\n185\t[source.session_detection]\n186\tmethod = \"delimiter\"\n187\tdelimiter_pattern = \"^---SESSION START---\"  # Regex matched against each line\n188\t```\n189\t\n190\t### `[parser]` — Field Mapping\n191\t\n192\tMaps fields from the agent's native format to AgentScribe's canonical event schema. The mapping syntax depends on the `format`.\n193\t\n194\t#### For `jsonl` and `json-tree` formats\n195\t\n196\tUse dot-notation paths to reference nested JSON fields:\n197\t\n198\t| Field       | Required | Description                              |\n199\t|-------------|----------|------------------------------------------|\n200\t| `timestamp` | yes      | Path to the timestamp field. Must be ISO 8601 or Unix epoch (ms). |\n201\t| `role`      | yes      | Path to the role field. Value must be one of: `user`, `assistant`, `system`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`. If the source uses different names, use `[parser.role_map]`. |\n202\t| `content`   | yes      | Path to the message content field.       |\n203\t| `type`      | no       | Path to an event type field. Used to filter which events to include (see `[parser.include_types]`). |\n204\t| `tool_name` | no       | Path to the tool/function name for tool call events. |\n205\t| `tool_args` | no       | Path to tool call arguments.             |\n206\t| `tokens_in` | no       | Path to input token count.               |\n207\t| `tokens_out`| no       | Path to output token count.              |\n208\t\n209\t**Dot-notation examples:**\n210\t```toml\n211\t# Flat structure: {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"hello\"}\n212\trole = \"role\"\n213\tcontent = \"content\"\n214\t\n215\t# Nested: {\"message\": {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": [{\"text\": \"hello\"}]}}\n216\trole = \"message.role\"\n217\tcontent = \"message.content[0].text\"\n218\t\n219\t# Array access: {\"parts\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"value\": \"hello\"}]}\n220\tcontent = \"parts[0].value\"\n221\t```\n222\t\n223\t#### For `markdown` format\n224\t\n225\tMarkdown parsing uses prefix-based role detection:\n226\t\n227\t| Field              | Required | Description                              |\n228\t|--------------------|----------|------------------------------------------|\n229\t| `user_prefix`      | yes      | Line prefix that identifies user messages (e.g., `\"#### \"`). |\n230\t| `assistant_prefix` | yes      | Line prefix for assistant messages. Use `\"\"` (empty string) if assistant text has no prefix. |\n231\t| `tool_prefix`      | no       | Line prefix for tool output (e.g., `\"> \"`). |\n232\t| `system_prefix`    | no       | Line prefix for system messages.         |\n233\t| `timestamp_pattern`| no       | Regex to extract timestamps from the log. Group 1 should capture the timestamp string. |\n234\t\n235\t#### For `sqlite` format\n236\t\n237\tSQLite parsing requires specifying the query to extract conversations. AgentScribe opens SQLite databases in read-only mode and never modifies them.\n238\t\n239\t| Field    | Required | Description                              |\n240\t|----------|----------|------------------------------------------|\n241\t| `query`  | yes      | SQL query that returns rows with the mapped fields. Use `{file}` as placeholder for the database path. |\n242\t| `key_filter` | no   | For key-value stores (like Cursor/Windsurf `state.vscdb`), the key pattern to read. When set, only rows whose key matches this pattern are selected. |\n243\t| `content_path` | no | JSONPath expression into the extracted value blob. Used when the database stores conversations as nested JSON blobs. Supports `[*]` for array access and dot-notation for nested fields. |\n244\t\n245\t**Agents using this format:** Cursor, Windsurf\n246\t\n247\t**Key-value stores (Cursor/Windsurf):**\n248\t\n249\tCursor and Windsurf store conversation data in a `state.vscdb` SQLite database as JSON blobs in a key-value table. Use `key_filter` to target the right keys:\n250\t\n251\t```toml\n252\t[plugin]\n253\tname = \"cursor\"\n254\tversion = \"1.0\"\n255\t\n256\t[source]\n257\tpaths = [\"~/.cursor/state.vscdb\", \"~/.windsurf/state.vscdb\"]\n258\tformat = \"sqlite\"\n259\t\n260\t[source.session_detection]\n261\tmethod = \"delimiter\"\n262\tdelimiter_pattern = \"^---TAB---\"    # Sessions are delimited within the JSON blob\n263\t\n264\t[parser]\n265\tquery = \"SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key = 'composerData'\"\n266\tkey_filter = \"composerData\"\n267\tcontent_path = \"tabs[*].messages[*]\"\n268\trole = \"role\"\n269\tcontent = \"content\"\n270\ttimestamp = \"timestamp\"\n271\t\n272\t[parser.static]\n273\tsource_agent = \"cursor\"\n274\t```\n275\t\n276\t**Direct table queries:**\n277\t\n278\tIf the database stores conversations in a regular table with structured columns:\n279\t\n280\t```toml\n281\t[plugin]\n282\tname = \"my-agent\"\n283\tversion = \"1.0\"\n284\t\n285\t[source]\n286\tpaths = [\"~/.my-agent/conversations.db\"]\n287\tformat = \"sqlite\"\n288\t\n289\t[source.session_detection]\n290\tmethod = \"field:session_id\"\n291\t\n292\t[parser]\n293\tquery = \"SELECT session_id, role, content, timestamp FROM messages ORDER BY timestamp\"\n294\trole = \"role\"\n295\tcontent = \"content\"\n296\ttimestamp = \"timestamp\"\n297\t\n298\t[parser.static]\n299\tsource_agent = \"my-agent\"\n300\t```\n301\t\n302\t**Note:** AgentScribe opens SQLite databases in read-only mode (`?mode=ro`). If you get \"database is locked\" errors, the source agent may have an exclusive lock — scrape when the agent is idle.\n303\t\n304\t### `[parser.role_map]` — Role Translation (Optional)\n305\t\n306\tIf the agent uses different names for roles, map them to AgentScribe's canonical roles:\n307\t\n308\t```toml\n309\t[parser.role_map]\n310\t\"human\" = \"user\"\n311\t\"ai\" = \"assistant\"\n312\t\"function_call\" = \"tool_call\"\n313\t\"function_result\" = \"tool_result\"\n314\t\"developer\" = \"system\"\n315\t```\n316\t\n317\t### `[parser.include_types]` — Event Filtering (Optional)\n318\t\n319\tIf the source contains event types you want to skip (progress events, file snapshots, etc.), specify which types to include:\n320\t\n321\t```toml\n322\t[parser.include_types]\n323\tfield = \"type\"\n324\tvalues = [\"user\", \"assistant\"]  # Only include these event types\n325\t```\n326\t\n327\tOr exclude specific types:\n328\t\n329\t```toml\n330\t[parser.exclude_types]\n331\tfield = \"type\"\n332\tvalues = [\"file-history-snapshot\", \"progress\"]\n333\t```\n334\t\n335\t### `[parser.static]` — Static Metadata (Optional)\n336\t\n337\tKey-value pairs applied to every event from this plugin. Use this for fields that are constant for the agent type:\n338\t\n339\t```toml\n340\t[parser.static]\n341\tsource_agent = \"my-agent\"\n342\tsource_version = \"2.1.0\"\n343\t```\n344\t\n345\t### `[metadata]` — Supplementary Data Sources (Optional)\n346\t\n347\tPaths to additional files that provide per-session metadata (token counts, summaries, outcomes). Supports `{session_id}` interpolation.\n348\t\n349\t```toml\n350\t[metadata]\n351\tsession_meta = \"~/.my-agent/meta/{session_id}.json\"\n352\tsession_summary = \"~/.my-agent/summaries/{session_id}.md\"\n353\t```\n354\t\n355\t| Field             | Required | Description                              |\n356\t|-------------------|----------|------------------------------------------|\n357\t| `session_meta`    | no       | JSON file with session-level metadata (duration, tokens, etc.). |\n358\t| `session_summary` | no       | Markdown or text file with a session summary. |\n359\t| `session_facets`  | no       | JSON file with LLM-generated session analysis. |\n360\t\n361\t---\n362\t\n363\t## Format Reference\n364\t\n365\t### `jsonl` — JSON Lines\n366\t\n367\tOne JSON object per line. Most common format. Each line is parsed independently and field-mapped.\n368\t\n369\t**Agents using this format:** Claude Code, Codex\n370\t\n371\t### `markdown` — Structured Markdown\n372\t\n373\tAppend-only Markdown where roles are distinguished by line prefixes (headings, blockquotes, bare text). The parser splits content by prefix and assigns roles.\n374\t\n375\t**Agents using this format:** Aider\n376\t\n377\t### `json-tree` — JSON File Hierarchy\n378\t\n379\tMultiple JSON files organized in a directory tree, where sessions/messages/parts are separate files linked by ID. The parser walks the tree and reassembles conversations.\n380\t\n381\t**Agents using this format:** OpenCode\n382\t\n383\tWhen using `json-tree`, add a `[source.tree]` section:\n384\t\n385\t```toml\n386\t[source.tree]\n387\tsession_glob = \"session/{projectId}/{sessionId}.json\"\n388\tmessage_glob = \"message/{sessionId}/{messageId}.json\"\n389\tpart_glob = \"part/{messageId}/{partId}.json\"\n390\tsession_id_field = \"id\"\n391\tmessage_session_field = \"sessionId\"\n392\tpart_message_field = \"messageId\"\n393\tordering_field = \"createdAt\"\n394\t```\n395\t\n396\t### `sqlite` — SQLite Database\n397\t\n398\tData stored in SQLite databases, often as JSON blobs in key-value tables. The parser runs a SQL query, extracts the result, and parses embedded JSON.\n399\t\n400\t**Agents using this format:** Cursor, Windsurf\n401\t\n402\t---\n403\t\n404\t## Canonical Event Schema (Target)\n405\t\n406\tEvery event your plugin produces is normalized into this schema. Your field mappings must resolve to these fields:\n407\t\n408\t```json\n409\t{\n410\t  \"ts\": \"2026-03-16T12:00:00Z\",\n411\t  \"session_id\": \"my-agent/abc123\",\n412\t  \"source_agent\": null,\n418\t  \"tokens\": {\"input\": 1200, \"output\": 450},\n419\t  \"tags\": [\"git\", \"migration\"]\n420\t}\n421\t```\n422\t\n423\t| Field            | Type   | Description                              |\n424\t|------------------|--------|------------------------------------------|\n425\t| `ts`             | string | ISO 8601 timestamp of the event          |\n426\t| `session_id`     | string | `<agent-name>/<id>` — auto-prefixed by AgentScribe |\n427\t| `source_agent`   | string | Plugin name (from `[parser.static]` or `[plugin].name`) |\n428\t| `source_version` | string | Agent version, |\n435\t\n436\t---\n437\t\n438\t## Walkthrough: Adding a New Agent\n439\t\n440\tSuppose a new coding agent called \"Pilot\" stores its logs as JSONL at `~/.pilot/sessions/<date>/<uuid>.jsonl` with Check `~` expansion and directory existence. |\n607\t| Wrong session boundaries | Incorrect `session_detection` method | Try `timestamp-gap` with a shorter threshold, or switch to `delimiter` if the log has markers. |\n608\t| Roles not mapping | Agent uses non-standard role names | Add a `[parser.role_map]` section. Run `--dry-run --output-events` to see raw role values. |\n609\t| Timestamps not parsing | Non-standard format | AgentScribe auto-detects ISO 8601 and Unix epoch (seconds and milliseconds). For other formats, file an issue. |\n610\t| Missing content | Wrong field path | Check dot-notation in `[parser]`. Use `--dry-run --output-events` to see what's being extracted. |\n611\t| SQLite locked | Agent is actively writing | AgentScribe opens SQLite in read-only mode (`?mode=ro`). If still locked, the agent may have an exclusive lock — scrape when the agent is idle. |\n612\t\n613\t---\n614\t\n615\t## Community Contribution Workflow\n616\t\n617\tIf you write a plugin for an agent that AgentScribe doesn't cover yet, you can share it with the community by submitting it to the `examples/` directory. A plugin teaches AgentScribe how to find, read, and normalize conversation logs from a specific coding agent.\n\n## What a Plugin Is\n\nA plugin is a single TOML file that declares:\n\n1. **Where** to find log files on disk\n2. **What format** the logs are in\n3. **How to detect session boundaries** within the logs\n4. **How to map fields** from the agent's native format to AgentScribe's canonical schema\n\nNo code is required. If your agent writes logs in a supported format (JSONL, Markdown, JSON tree, SQLite), you only need a TOML file.\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start\n\nCreate a file at `~/.agentscribe/plugins/<agent-name>.toml`:\n\n```toml\n[plugin]\nname = \"my-agent\"\nversion = \"1.0\"\n\n[source]\npaths = [\"~/.my-agent/history/*.jsonl\"]\nformat = \"jsonl\"\n\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"one-file-per-session\"\nsession_id_from = \"filename\"\n\n[parser]\ntimestamp = \"timestamp\"\nrole = \"role\"\ncontent = \"content\"\n\n[parser.static]\nsource_agent = \"my-agent\"\n```\n\nValidate it:\n\n```bash\nagentscribe plugins validate ~/.agentscribe/plugins/my-agent.toml\n```\n\nTest a scrape:\n\n```bash\nagentscribe scrape --plugin my-agent --dry-run\n```\n\n---\n\n## Plugin Specification\n\n### `[plugin]` — Identity\n\n| Field     | Required | Description                              |\n|-----------|----------|------------------------------------------|\n| `name`    | yes      | Unique identifier for this agent type. Used in session IDs, CLI filters, and output directory names. Must be lowercase, alphanumeric, and hyphens only. |\n| `version` | yes      | Plugin definition version. Increment when you change the field mapping or source paths. AgentScribe uses this to detect when re-scraping is needed. |\n\n### `[source]` — Where to Find Logs\n\n| Field     | Required | Description                              |\n|-----------|----------|------------------------------------------|\n| `paths`   | yes      | Array of glob patterns pointing to log files. Supports `~` (home dir), `$ENV_VAR` expansion, and standard glob syntax (`*`, `**`, `?`). |\n| `exclude` | no       | Array of glob patterns to exclude from matches. Evaluated after `paths`. |\n| `format`  | yes      | Log file format. One of: `jsonl`, `markdown`, `json-tree`, `sqlite`. See [Format Reference](#format-reference) below. |\n\n**Path examples:**\n```toml\n# Single known location\npaths = [\"~/.my-agent/conversations/*.jsonl\"]\n\n# Multiple search roots for project-local files\npaths = [\"~/projects/*/.my-agent.log\", \"~/repos/*/.my-agent.log\"]\n\n# Recursive search\npaths = [\"~/.my-agent/**/session-*.json\"]\n\n# Environment variable expansion\npaths = [\"$MY_AGENT_DATA_DIR/logs/*.jsonl\"]\n```\n\n### `[source.envelope]` — Envelope Unwrapping (Optional)\n\nFor JSONL sources where each line is wrapped in an envelope structure (e.g., `{timestamp, type, payload}`), configure envelope unwrapping to extract the actual event payload.\n\n```toml\n[source.envelope]\npayload_field = \"data\"     # Field containing the event payload object\ntype_field = \"type\"        # Field containing the event type for routing\n\n[source.envelope.type_routing]\n\"message\" = \"event\"       # Parse as regular event\n\"metadata\" = \"meta\"        # Session metadata (not an event)\n\"heartbeat\" = \"skip\"      # Skip this type entirely\n```\n\n**Routing actions:**\n- `event` - Extract the payload and parse it as a regular event using `[parser]` field mappings\n- `meta` - Session-level metadata (for future use; currently skipped)\n- `skip` - Ignore this line entirely\n\n**Envelope-level field access:**\nUse the `^` prefix in field mappings to access fields from the envelope wrapper instead of the payload:\n\n```toml\n[parser]\ntimestamp = \"^timestamp\"  # From envelope: {\"timestamp\": \"...\", \"type\": \"...\", \"data\": {...}}\nrole = \"role\"             # From payload: {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"...\"}\ncontent = \"content\"\n```\n\n**Unknown types:** Any type value not in `type_routing` defaults to `skip` with a warning.\n\n**Example (Codex rollouts):**\n```json\n{\"timestamp\": \"2026-03-16T12:00:00Z\", \"type\": \"message\", \"data\": {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Fix the bug\"}}\n{\"timestamp\": \"2026-03-16T12:00:05Z\", \"type\": \"metadata\", \"data\": {\"model\": \"gpt-4\"}}\n{\"timestamp\": \"2026-03-16T12:00:10Z\", \"type\": \"heartbeat\", \"data\": {\"status\": \"ok\"}}\n```\n\n```toml\n[source.envelope]\npayload_field = \"data\"\ntype_field = \"type\"\n\n[source.envelope.type_routing]\n\"message\" = \"event\"\n\"metadata\" = \"meta\"\n\"heartbeat\" = \"skip\"\n\n[parser]\ntimestamp = \"^timestamp\"\nrole = \"role\"\ncontent = \"content\"\n```\n\n### `[source.session_detection]` — Session Boundaries\n\nAgents store sessions differently. Some create one file per session. Others append to a single continuous file. This section tells AgentScribe how to split logs into discrete sessions.\n\n| Field              | Required | Description                              |\n|--------------------|----------|------------------------------------------|\n| `method`           | yes      | Detection strategy. One of: `one-file-per-session`, `timestamp-gap`, `delimiter`. |\n| `session_id_from`  | depends  | Where to extract the session ID. Required for `one-file-per-session`. |\n| `gap_threshold`    | depends  | Time gap that signals a new session. Required for `timestamp-gap`. Format: `\"30m\"`, `\"2h\"`, `\"1d\"`. |\n| `delimiter_pattern`| depends  | Regex pattern that marks session boundaries. Required for `delimiter`. |\n\n**Method: `one-file-per-session`**\n\nEach log file is one session. Most agents work this way.\n\n```toml\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"one-file-per-session\"\nsession_id_from = \"filename\"     # Use the filename (minus extension) as session ID\n# OR\nsession_id_from = \"field:sessionId\"  # Extract from a JSON field in the first line\n```\n\n**Method: `timestamp-gap`**\n\nFor agents that append to a single file (e.g., Aider). A new session starts when the gap between consecutive entries exceeds the threshold.\n\n```toml\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"timestamp-gap\"\ngap_threshold = \"30m\"\n```\n\nNote: requires the `timestamp` field mapping in `[parser]` to work. If the source format has no timestamps, use `delimiter` instead.\n\n**Method: `delimiter`**\n\nSplit on a pattern in the log content. Useful for agents that write explicit session markers.\n\n```toml\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"delimiter\"\ndelimiter_pattern = \"^---SESSION START---\"  # Regex matched against each line\n```\n\n### `[parser]` — Field Mapping\n\nMaps fields from the agent's native format to AgentScribe's canonical event schema. The mapping syntax depends on the `format`.\n\n#### For `jsonl` and `json-tree` formats\n\nUse dot-notation paths to reference nested JSON fields:\n\n| Field       | Required | Description                              |\n|-------------|----------|------------------------------------------|\n| `timestamp` | yes      | Path to the timestamp field. Must be ISO 8601 or Unix epoch (ms). |\n| `role`      | yes      | Path to the role field. Value must be one of: `user`, `assistant`, `system`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`. If the source uses different names, use `[parser.role_map]`. |\n| `content`   | yes      | Path to the message content field.       |\n| `type`      | no       | Path to an event type field. Used to filter which events to include (see `[parser.include_types]`). |\n| `tool_name` | no       | Path to the tool/function name for tool call events. |\n| `tool_args` | no       | Path to tool call arguments.             |\n| `tokens_in` | no       | Path to input token count.               |\n| `tokens_out`| no       | Path to output token count.              |\n\n**Dot-notation examples:**\n```toml\n# Flat structure: {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"hello\"}\nrole = \"role\"\ncontent = \"content\"\n\n# Nested: {\"message\": {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": [{\"text\": \"hello\"}]}}\nrole = \"message.role\"\ncontent = \"message.content[0].text\"\n\n# Array access: {\"parts\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"value\": \"hello\"}]}\ncontent = \"parts[0].value\"\n```\n\n#### For `markdown` format\n\nMarkdown parsing uses prefix-based role detection:\n\n| Field              | Required | Description                              |\n|--------------------|----------|------------------------------------------|\n| `user_prefix`      | yes      | Line prefix that identifies user messages (e.g., `\"#### \"`). |\n| `assistant_prefix` | yes      | Line prefix for assistant messages. Use `\"\"` (empty string) if assistant text has no prefix. |\n| `tool_prefix`      | no       | Line prefix for tool output (e.g., `\"> \"`). |\n| `system_prefix`    | no       | Line prefix for system messages.         |\n| `timestamp_pattern`| no       | Regex to extract timestamps from the log. Group 1 should capture the timestamp string. |\n\n#### For `sqlite` format\n\nSQLite parsing requires specifying the query to extract conversations. AgentScribe opens SQLite databases in read-only mode and never modifies them.\n\n| Field    | Required | Description                              |\n|----------|----------|------------------------------------------|\n| `query`  | yes      | SQL query that returns rows with the mapped fields. Use `{file}` as placeholder for the database path. |\n| `key_filter` | no   | For key-value stores (like Cursor/Windsurf `state.vscdb`), the key pattern to read. When set, only rows whose key matches this pattern are selected. |\n| `content_path` | no | JSONPath expression into the extracted value blob. Used when the database stores conversations as nested JSON blobs. Supports `[*]` for array access and dot-notation for nested fields. |\n\n**Agents using this format:** Cursor, Windsurf\n\n**Key-value stores (Cursor/Windsurf):**\n\nCursor and Windsurf store conversation data in a `state.vscdb` SQLite database as JSON blobs in a key-value table. Use `key_filter` to target the right keys:\n\n```toml\n[plugin]\nname = \"cursor\"\nversion = \"1.0\"\n\n[source]\npaths = [\"~/.cursor/state.vscdb\", \"~/.windsurf/state.vscdb\"]\nformat = \"sqlite\"\n\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"delimiter\"\ndelimiter_pattern = \"^---TAB---\"    # Sessions are delimited within the JSON blob\n\n[parser]\nquery = \"SELECT value FROM ItemTable WHERE key = 'composerData'\"\nkey_filter = \"composerData\"\ncontent_path = \"tabs[*].messages[*]\"\nrole = \"role\"\ncontent = \"content\"\ntimestamp = \"timestamp\"\n\n[parser.static]\nsource_agent = \"cursor\"\n```\n\n**Direct table queries:**\n\nIf the database stores conversations in a regular table with structured columns:\n\n```toml\n[plugin]\nname = \"my-agent\"\nversion = \"1.0\"\n\n[source]\npaths = [\"~/.my-agent/conversations.db\"]\nformat = \"sqlite\"\n\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"field:session_id\"\n\n[parser]\nquery = \"SELECT session_id, role, content, timestamp FROM messages ORDER BY timestamp\"\nrole = \"role\"\ncontent = \"content\"\ntimestamp = \"timestamp\"\n\n[parser.static]\nsource_agent = \"my-agent\"\n```\n\n**Note:** AgentScribe opens SQLite databases in read-only mode (`?mode=ro`). If you get \"database is locked\" errors, the source agent may have an exclusive lock — scrape when the agent is idle.\n\n### `[parser.role_map]` — Role Translation (Optional)\n\nIf the agent uses different names for roles, map them to AgentScribe's canonical roles:\n\n```toml\n[parser.role_map]\n\"human\" = \"user\"\n\"ai\" = \"assistant\"\n\"function_call\" = \"tool_call\"\n\"function_result\" = \"tool_result\"\n\"developer\" = \"system\"\n```\n\n### `[parser.include_types]` — Event Filtering (Optional)\n\nIf the source contains event types you want to skip (progress events, file snapshots, etc.), specify which types to include:\n\n```toml\n[parser.include_types]\nfield = \"type\"\nvalues = [\"user\", \"assistant\"]  # Only include these event types\n```\n\nOr exclude specific types:\n\n```toml\n[parser.exclude_types]\nfield = \"type\"\nvalues = [\"file-history-snapshot\", \"progress\"]\n```\n\n### `[parser.static]` — Static Metadata (Optional)\n\nKey-value pairs applied to every event from this plugin. Use this for fields that are constant for the agent type:\n\n```toml\n[parser.static]\nsource_agent = \"my-agent\"\nsource_version = \"2.1.0\"\n```\n\n### `[metadata]` — Supplementary Data Sources (Optional)\n\nPaths to additional files that provide per-session metadata (token counts, summaries, outcomes). Supports `{session_id}` interpolation.\n\n```toml\n[metadata]\nsession_meta = \"~/.my-agent/meta/{session_id}.json\"\nsession_summary = \"~/.my-agent/summaries/{session_id}.md\"\n```\n\n| Field             | Required | Description                              |\n|-------------------|----------|------------------------------------------|\n| `session_meta`    | no       | JSON file with session-level metadata (duration, tokens, etc.). |\n| `session_summary` | no       | Markdown or text file with a session summary. |\n| `session_facets`  | no       | JSON file with LLM-generated session analysis. |\n\n---\n\n## Format Reference\n\n### `jsonl` — JSON Lines\n\nOne JSON object per line. Most common format. Each line is parsed independently and field-mapped.\n\n**Agents using this format:** Claude Code, Codex\n\n### `markdown` — Structured Markdown\n\nAppend-only Markdown where roles are distinguished by line prefixes (headings, blockquotes, bare text). The parser splits content by prefix and assigns roles.\n\n**Agents using this format:** Aider\n\n### `json-tree` — JSON File Hierarchy\n\nMultiple JSON files organized in a directory tree, where sessions/messages/parts are separate files linked by ID. The parser walks the tree and reassembles conversations.\n\n**Agents using this format:** OpenCode\n\nWhen using `json-tree`, add a `[source.tree]` section:\n\n```toml\n[source.tree]\nsession_glob = \"session/{projectId}/{sessionId}.json\"\nmessage_glob = \"message/{sessionId}/{messageId}.json\"\npart_glob = \"part/{messageId}/{partId}.json\"\nsession_id_field = \"id\"\nmessage_session_field = \"sessionId\"\npart_message_field = \"messageId\"\nordering_field = \"createdAt\"\n```\n\n### `sqlite` — SQLite Database\n\nData stored in SQLite databases, often as JSON blobs in key-value tables. The parser runs a SQL query, extracts the result, and parses embedded JSON.\n\n**Agents using this format:** Cursor, Windsurf\n\n---\n\n## Canonical Event Schema (Target)\n\nEvery event your plugin produces is normalized into this schema. Your field mappings must resolve to these fields:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"ts\": \"2026-03-16T12:00:00Z\",\n  \"session_id\": \"my-agent/abc123\",\n  \"source_agent\": \"my-agent\",\n  \"source_version\": \"2.1.0\",\n  \"project\": \"/home/user/myproject\",\n  \"role\": \"user\",\n  \"content\": \"the message text\",\n  \"tool\": null,\n  \"tokens\": {\"input\": 1200, \"output\": 450},\n  \"tags\": [\"git\", \"migration\"]\n}\n```\n\n| Field            | Type   | Description                              |\n|------------------|--------|------------------------------------------|\n| `ts`             | string | ISO 8601 timestamp of the event          |\n| `session_id`     | string | `<agent-name>/<id>` — auto-prefixed by AgentScribe |\n| `source_agent`   | string | Plugin name (from `[parser.static]` or `[plugin].name`) |\n| `source_version` | string | Agent version, if available              |\n| `project`        | string | Absolute path to the project directory   |\n| `role`           | string | One of: `user`, `assistant`, `system`, `tool_call`, `tool_result` |\n| `content`        | string | The message/event text content           |\n| `tool`           | string | Tool name (for `tool_call`/`tool_result` roles), null otherwise |\n| `tokens`         | object | `{input, output}` token counts, null if unavailable |\n| `tags`           | array  | Extracted tags (auto-generated during indexing) |\n\n---\n\n## Walkthrough: Adding a New Agent\n\nSuppose a new coding agent called \"Pilot\" stores its logs as JSONL at `~/.pilot/sessions/<date>/<uuid>.jsonl` with this line format:\n\n```json\n{\"time\": 1710590400, \"id\": \"msg_001\", \"session\": \"abc-123\", \"speaker\": \"human\", \"text\": \"Fix the login bug\", \"input_tokens\": 50, \"output_tokens\": 0}\n{\"time\": 1710590420, \"id\": \"msg_002\", \"session\": \"abc-123\", \"speaker\": \"ai\", \"text\": \"I'll look at auth.py...\", \"input_tokens\": 0, \"output_tokens\": 200}\n```\n\n**Step 1:** Create the plugin file:\n\n```toml\n# ~/.agentscribe/plugins/pilot.toml\n\n[plugin]\nname = \"pilot\"\nversion = \"1.0\"\n\n[source]\npaths = [\"~/.pilot/sessions/**/*.jsonl\"]\nformat = \"jsonl\"\n\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"one-file-per-session\"\nsession_id_from = \"filename\"\n\n[parser]\ntimestamp = \"time\"               # Unix epoch — AgentScribe auto-detects epoch vs ISO 8601\nrole = \"speaker\"\ncontent = \"text\"\ntokens_in = \"input_tokens\"\ntokens_out = \"output_tokens\"\n\n[parser.role_map]\n\"human\" = \"user\"\n\"ai\" = \"assistant\"\n\n[parser.exclude_types]\nfield = \"speaker\"\nvalues = [\"system_internal\"]     # Skip internal system events if present\n\n[parser.static]\nsource_agent = \"pilot\"\n```\n\n**Step 2:** Validate:\n\n```bash\nagentscribe plugins validate ~/.agentscribe/plugins/pilot.toml\n```\n\nValidation checks:\n- All required fields present\n- `paths` globs resolve to at least one file\n- `format` is a supported type\n- Field mappings reference valid dot-notation paths\n- `role_map` target values are valid canonical roles\n- No conflicting `include_types` / `exclude_types`\n\n**Step 3:** Dry-run scrape:\n\n```bash\nagentscribe scrape --plugin pilot --dry-run\n```\n\nThis shows what sessions would be scraped without writing any files. Review the output to confirm:\n- Correct number of sessions detected\n- Session boundaries are right\n- Fields map correctly (timestamps parse, roles resolve)\n\n**Step 4:** Full scrape:\n\n```bash\nagentscribe scrape --plugin pilot\n```\n\n**Step 5:** Verify:\n\n```bash\nagentscribe status\n# Should show \"pilot\" with session count and last scrape time\n\nagentscribe search \"login bug\" --plugin pilot\n# Should find the session from the example above\n```\n\n---\n\n## Common Patterns\n\n### Agent that appends to a single file per project\n\n```toml\n[source]\npaths = [\"~/projects/*/.agent-history.log\"]\nformat = \"jsonl\"\n\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"timestamp-gap\"\ngap_threshold = \"1h\"\n```\n\n### Agent with structured directories but no timestamps\n\n```toml\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"one-file-per-session\"\nsession_id_from = \"filename\"\n# AgentScribe falls back to file modification time when no timestamp field is available\n```\n\n### Agent that uses delimiters between sessions\n\n```toml\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"delimiter\"\ndelimiter_pattern = \"^={3,}\\\\s*New Session\"\n```\n\n### Agent with sub-agent / sub-conversation logs\n\n```toml\n# Main conversations\n[source]\npaths = [\"~/.agent/sessions/*.jsonl\"]\nexclude = [\"*/sub-agents/*\"]\n\n# Optionally create a second plugin for sub-agents\n# ~/.agentscribe/plugins/my-agent-subagents.toml\n```\n\n### Filtering to only conversation events\n\nMany agents log internal events (file snapshots, progress updates) alongside conversation turns. Use type filtering to keep only what matters:\n\n```toml\n[parser.include_types]\nfield = \"event_type\"\nvalues = [\"message\", \"tool_call\", \"tool_result\"]\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing Your Plugin\n\n```bash\n# Validate the TOML structure and field references\nagentscribe plugins validate <plugin-file>\n\n# Dry-run: show what would be scraped without writing\nagentscribe scrape --plugin <name> --dry-run\n\n# Scrape a single file to verify parsing\nagentscribe scrape --plugin <name> --file <path-to-one-log-file>\n\n# Show parsed events as JSON (for inspecting field mapping)\nagentscribe scrape --plugin <name> --dry-run --output-events\n\n# List all registered plugins and their status\nagentscribe plugins list\n```\n\n---\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n| Problem | Likely Cause | Fix |\n|---------|-------------|-----|\n| No files found | `paths` globs don't match | Run `agentscribe plugins validate` — it reports glob match counts. Check `~` expansion and directory existence. |\n| Wrong session boundaries | Incorrect `session_detection` method | Try `timestamp-gap` with a shorter threshold, or switch to `delimiter` if the log has markers. |\n| Roles not mapping | Agent uses non-standard role names | Add a `[parser.role_map]` section. Run `--dry-run --output-events` to see raw role values. |\n| Timestamps not parsing | Non-standard format | AgentScribe auto-detects ISO 8601 and Unix epoch (seconds and milliseconds). For other formats, file an issue. |\n| Missing content | Wrong field path | Check dot-notation in `[parser]`. Use `--dry-run --output-events` to see what's being extracted. |\n| SQLite locked | Agent is actively writing | AgentScribe opens SQLite in read-only mode (`?mode=ro`). If still locked, the agent may have an exclusive lock — scrape when the agent is idle. |\n\n---\n\n## Community Contribution Workflow\n\nIf you write a plugin for an agent that AgentScribe doesn't cover yet, you can share it with the community by submitting it to the `examples/` directory. This is separate from the bundled plugins (which require deeper integration testing); contributed examples are lower-friction and easier to accept.\n\n### Where to put it\n\nCommunity plugins live in `examples/` at the repository root (not in `plugins/`, which is reserved for bundled plugins). See `examples/README.md` for the current list of contributed plugins.\n\n### Contribution checklist\n\nBefore opening a pull request, confirm:\n\n- [ ] Plugin validates cleanly: `agentscribe plugins validate examples/<agent-name>.toml`\n- [ ] Dry-run shows correct session and event counts against real log files\n- [ ] `name` is lowercase, alphanumeric + hyphens (e.g., `my-agent`)\n- [ ] `version` is `\"1.0\"` for a new plugin\n- [ ] `paths` covers all common platform locations (Linux, macOS, Windows if applicable)\n- [ ] Non-obvious field choices or version dependencies are explained in comments\n- [ ] No hardcoded absolute paths specific to your machine\n- [ ] A row has been added to the table in `examples/README.md`\n\n### Versioning your plugin\n\nIncrement `version` in the `[plugin]` section whenever you change field mappings or source paths. AgentScribe uses this value to detect when previously-scraped files need to be re-processed.\n\n```toml\n[plugin]\nname    = \"my-agent\"\nversion = \"1.1\"   # bumped: added token_in / token_out mappings\n```\n\n### Submitting\n\n1. Fork the repository.\n2. Add your plugin as `examples/<agent-name>.toml`.\n3. Add a row to `examples/README.md`.\n4. Open a pull request with a brief description of the agent, how you tested the plugin, and which platform(s) you verified path expansion on.\n\nMaintainers will review field mapping quality, path coverage across platforms, and session detection accuracy before merging.\n","numLines":654,"startLine":1,"totalLines":654}}}

payload with None envelope to signal \"drop this line\"\n            (serde_json::json!({}), None)\n        }\n        \"meta\" => {\n            // Return empty payload but preserve the envelope wrapper for metadata extraction\n            (serde_json::json!({}), Some(raw_json.clone()))\n        }\n        \"event\" => {\n            // Extract payload from payload_field\n            let extracted = raw_json.get(&envelope.payload_field).and_then(|v| {\n                // Only use if it's an object (not a string/null/etc)\n                match v {\n                    Value::Object(_) => Some(v),\n                    _ => None,\n                }\n            });\n\n            match extracted {\n                Some(payload) => {\n                    // Return the extracted payload along with the envelope wrapper\n                    (payload.clone(), Some(raw_json.clone()))\n                }\n                None => {\n                    // Missing or non-object payload_field - skip with warning\n                    eprintln!(\n                        \"Warning: Envelope payload_field '{}' missing or not an object for type '{}', skipping line\",\n                        envelope.payload_field, type_value\n                    );\n                    (serde_json::json!({}), None)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        _ => {\n            // Unknown routing (shouldn't happen due to get_routing defaults, but handle defensively)\n            (serde_json::json!({}), None)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Opens a file, optionally decompressing if it has a .zst extension\nfn open_file_maybe_zst(path: &Path) -> Result<Box<dyn BufRead>> {\n    let file = std::fs::File::open(path)?;\n\n    if path.extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) == Some(\"zst\") {\n        // Use streaming zstd decompression\n        let decoder =\n            zstd::stream::read::Decoder::new(file).map_err(|e| AgentScribeError::Parse {\n                file: path.display().to_string(),\n                line: Some(0),\n                message: format!(\"Zstd decompression error: {}\", e),\n            })?;\n        Ok(Box::new(BufReader::new(decoder)))\n    } else {\n        Ok(Box::new(BufReader::new(file)))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl JsonlParser {\n    /// Parse a single JSONL line into an event\n    pub fn parse_line(\n        line: &str,\n        line_number: usize,\n        context: &ParseContext,\n        plugin: &Plugin,\n    ) -> Result<Vec<Event>> {\n        let raw_json: Value = serde_json::from_str(line).map_err(|e| {\n            AgentScribeError::parse_error_with_line(\n                &context.source_file,\n                line_number,\n                format!(\"Invalid JSON: {}\", e),\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        // --- Envelope routing and payload unwrapping ---\n        // When the plugin defines [source.envelope], the JSONL line is a wrapper:\n        //   { type_field: \"...\", payload_field: { ... actual event ... } }\n        // Type routing determines whether to produce events, skip, or capture metadata.\n        //\n        // Set up envelope_json and payload_json references:\n        // - envelope_json: reference to the full parsed line (or None if no envelope)\n        // - payload_json: reference to the event data (from payload_field if envelope, else full line)\n        //\n        // Field extraction uses envelope-aware functions:\n        // - Fields starting with '^' read from envelope_json\n        // - Fields without '^' read from payload_json\n\n        let (envelope_json, payload_json): (Option<&Value>, &Value) = if let Some(\n            ref envelope_cfg,\n        ) = plugin.source.envelope\n        {\n            // Envelope mode: extract type and apply routing\n            let type_value =\n                extract_string(&raw_json, &envelope_cfg.type_field).unwrap_or_default();\n            let routing = envelope_cfg.get_routing(&type_value);\n\n            match routing {\n                \"skip\" => {\n                    // Skip this line - no event emitted\n                    return Ok(Vec::new());\n                }\n                \"meta\" => {\n                    // Metadata line - no event emitted (future: session metadata accumulation)\n                    return Ok(Vec::new());\n                }\n                \"event\" => {\n                    // Extract payload from payload_field for event body\n                    let extracted = raw_json.get(&envelope_cfg.payload_field).and_then(|v| {\n                        // Only use if it's an object (not a string/null/etc)\n                        match v {\n                            Value::Object(_) => Some(v),\n                            _ => None,\n                        }\n                    });\n\n                    match extracted {\n                        Some(payload) => {\n                            // Valid payload object extracted\n                            (Some(&raw_json), payload)\n                        }\n                        None => {\n                            // Missing or non-object payload_field - skip with warning\n                            eprintln!(\n                                    \"Warning: Envelope payload_field '{}' missing or not an object for type '{}', skipping line\",\n                                    envelope_cfg.payload_field, type_value\n                                );\n                            return Ok(Vec::new());\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                _ => {\n                    // Unknown routing (shouldn't happen due to get_routing defaults, but handle defensively)\n                    return Ok(Vec::new());\n                }\n            }\n        } else {\n            // No envelope: both envelope_json and payload_json point to the full line\n            (None, &raw_json)\n        };\n\n        // Check type filter (envelope-aware: ^ prefix reads from wrapper, otherwise from payload)\n        if let Some(ref filter) = plugin.parser.include_types {\n            let type_field = &filter.field;\n            if let Some(type_val) =\n                extract_string_with_envelope(type_field, payload_json, envelope_json)\n            {\n                if !filter.values.contains(&type_val) {\n                    return Ok(Vec::new()); // Skip this event\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref filter) = plugin.parser.exclude_types {\n            let type_field = &filter.field;\n            if let Some(type_val) =\n                extract_string_with_envelope(type_field, payload_json, envelope_json)\n            {\n                if filter.values.contains(&type_val) {\n                    return Ok(Vec::new()); // Skip this event\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Parse timestamp (envelope-aware: ^ prefix reads from wrapper, otherwise from payload)\n        let ts = if let Some(ref ts_field) = plugin.parser.timestamp {\n            parse_timestamp_with_envelope(ts_field, payload_json, envelope_json).map_err(|e| {\n                AgentScribeError::parse_error_with_line(\n                    &context.source_file,\n                    line_number,\n                    format!(\"Timestamp error: {}\", e),\n                )\n            })?\n        } else {\n            Utc::now() // Fallback - shouldn't happen with validation\n        };\n\n        // Parse role (envelope-aware: ^ prefix reads from wrapper, otherwise from payload)\n        let role_str = if let Some(ref role_field) = plugin.parser.role {\n            extract_string_with_envelope(role_field, payload_json, envelope_json).ok_or_else(\n                || {\n                    AgentScribeError::parse_error_with_line(\n                        &context.source_file,\n                        line_number,\n                        format!(\"Role field '{}' not found\", role_field),\n                    )\n                },\n            )?\n        } else {\n            return Err(AgentScribeError::parse_error_with_line(\n                &context.source_file,\n                line_number,\n                \"No role field configured\".to_string(),\n            ));\n        };\n\n        // Apply role mapping\n        let role = if let Some(mapped) = plugin.parser.role_map.get(&role_str) {\n            Role::from_str(mapped).ok_or_else(|| {\n                AgentScribeError::parse_error_with_line(\n                    &context.source_file,\n                    line_number,\n                    format!(\"Invalid role mapping: {}\", mapped),\n                )\n            })?\n        } else {\n            Role::from_str(&role_str).ok_or_else(|| {\n                AgentScribeError::parse_error_with_line(\n                    &context.source_file,\n                    line_number,\n                    format!(\"Invalid role: {}\", role_str),\n                )\n            })?\n        };\n\n        // Parse content (envelope-aware: ^ prefix reads from wrapper, otherwise from payload)\n        let content = if let Some(ref content_field) = plugin.parser.content {\n            extract_string_with_envelope(content_field, payload_json, envelope_json)\n                .unwrap_or_default()\n        } else {\n            return Err(AgentScribeError::parse_error_with_line(\n                &context.source_file,\n                line_number,\n                \"No content field configured\".to_string(),\n            ));\n        };\n\n        // Build base event\n        let mut event = Event::new(\n            ts,\n            context.session_id.clone(),\n            context.source_agent.clone(),\n            role,\n            content,\n        );\n\n        // Extract tool name if applicable (envelope-aware: ^ prefix reads from wrapper, otherwise from payload)\n        if role == Role::ToolCall || role == Role::ToolResult {\n            if let Some(ref tool_field) = plugin.parser.tool_name {\n                if let Some(tool_name) =\n                    extract_string_with_envelope(tool_field, payload_json, envelope_json)\n                {\n                    event.tool = Some(tool_name);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Extract tokens (envelope-aware: ^ prefix reads from wrapper, otherwise from payload)\n        let tokens_in = plugin.parser.tokens_in.as_ref().and_then(|f| {\n            extract_string_with_envelope(f, payload_json, envelope_json)\n                .and_then(|s| s.parse::<u32>().ok())\n        });\n        let tokens_out = plugin.parser.tokens_out.as_ref().and_then(|f| {\n            extract_string_with_envelope(f, payload_json, envelope_json)\n                .and_then(|s| s.parse::<u32>().ok())\n        });\n\n        if tokens_in.is_some() || tokens_out.is_some() {\n            event.tokens = Some(TokenCounts {\n                input: tokens_in.unwrap_or(0),\n                output: tokens_out.unwrap_or(0),\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Set project from context\n        event.project = context.project.clone();\n\n        // Set model from context\n        event.model = context.model.clone();\n\n        // Add static fields\n        for (key, value) in &plugin.parser.static_fields {\n            match key.as_str() {\n                \"source_agent\" => {\n                    if let Some(s) = value.as_str() {\n                        event.source_agent = s.to_string();\n                    }\n                }\n                \"source_version\" => {\n                    if let Some(s) = value.as_str() {\n                        event.source_version = Some(s.to_string());\n                    }\n                }\n                _ => {}\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Handle event expansion for compound events (e.g., Claude Code tool_use blocks)\n        // For now, return single event - expansion can be added per-agent\n        Ok(vec![event])\n    }\n}\n\nimpl super::FormatParser for JsonlParser {\n    fn parse(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>> {\n        let reader = open_file_maybe_zst(source_path)?;\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n        // Get session ID from filename\n        let session_id = match &plugin.source.session_detection {\n            SessionDetection::OneFilePerSession { session_id_from } => {\n                match session_id_from {\n                    SessionIdSource::Filename => source_path\n                        .file_stem()\n                        .and_then(|s| s.to_str())\n                        .unwrap_or(\"unknown\")\n                        .to_string(),\n                    SessionIdSource::Field(_) => {\n                        // Need to read first line to get session ID\n                        \"unknown\".to_string() // Will be updated during parsing\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            _ => \"unknown\".to_string(),\n        };\n\n        let context = ParseContext::new(\n            session_id,\n            plugin.plugin.name.clone(),\n            source_path.display().to_string(),\n        );\n\n        for (line_num, line_result) in reader.lines().enumerate() {\n            let line_num = line_num + 1;\n            let line = match line_result {\n                Ok(l) => l,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    eprintln!(\n                        \"Warning: Read error at {}:{} - {}\",\n                        source_path.display(),\n                        line_num,\n                        e\n                    );\n                    continue;\n                }\n            };\n\n            if line.trim().is_empty() {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            match JsonlParser::parse_line(&line, line_num, &context, plugin) {\n                Ok(mut line_events) => events.append(&mut line_events),\n                Err(e) => {\n                    if e.is_skippable() {\n                        eprintln!(\"Warning: {}\", e);\n                    } else {\n                        return Err(e);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(events)\n    }\n\n    fn detect_sessions(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<SessionInfo>> {\n        // For JSONL with one-file-per-session, the file itself is the session\n        match &plugin.source.session_detection {\n            SessionDetection::OneFilePerSession { session_id_from } => {\n                let session_id = match session_id_from {\n                    SessionIdSource::Filename => source_path\n                        .file_stem()\n                        .and_then(|s| s.to_str())\n                        .unwrap_or(\"unknown\")\n                        .to_string(),\n                    SessionIdSource::Field(field) => {\n                        // Read first line to extract session ID (handle zst)\n                        match open_file_maybe_zst(source_path) {\n                            Ok(mut reader) => {\n                                let mut first_line = String::new();\n                                if reader.read_line(&mut first_line).is_ok() {\n                                    if let Ok(json) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&first_line) {\n                                        // Envelope-aware session ID extraction\n                                        // Check if we have envelope config\n                                        let (envelope_json, payload_json) = if let Some(\n                                            ref envelope_cfg,\n                                        ) =\n                                            plugin.source.envelope\n                                        {\n                                            let type_value =\n                                                extract_string(&json, &envelope_cfg.type_field)\n                                                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                                            let routing = envelope_cfg.get_routing(&type_value);\n\n                                            // Only extract if this line has routing\n                                            if routing == \"event\" || routing == \"meta\" {\n                                                let extracted = json\n                                                    .get(&envelope_cfg.payload_field)\n                                                    .and_then(|v| match v {\n                                                        Value::Object(_) => Some(v),\n                                                        _ => None,\n                                                    });\n                                                match extracted {\n                                                    Some(payload) => (Some(&json), payload),\n                                                    None => (None, &json),\n                                                }\n                                            } else {\n                                                (None, &json)\n                                            }\n                                        } else {\n                                            (None, &json)\n                                        };\n\n                                        extract_string_with_envelope(\n                                            field,\n                                            payload_json,\n                                            envelope_json,\n                                        )\n                                        .unwrap_or_else(|| \"unknown\".to_string())\n                                    } else {\n                                        \"unknown\".to_string()\n                                    }\n                                } else {\n                                    \"unknown\".to_string()\n                                }\n                            }\n                            Err(_) => \"unknown\".to_string(),\n                        }\n                    }\n                };\n\n                let file_size = std::fs::metadata(source_path)?.len();\n\n                // Detect subagent sessions and extract parent_session_id from directory structure\n                // Subagent files are at: ~/.claude/projects/<path>/<parent-session-uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl\n                let parent_session_id = source_path\n                    .components()\n                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                    .iter()\n                    .position(|c| c.as_os_str() == \"subagents\")\n                    .and_then(|subagents_idx| {\n                        // Parent session UUID is the component before \"subagents\"\n                        if subagents_idx > 0 {\n                            source_path\n                                .components()\n                                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                                .get(subagents_idx - 1)\n                                .and_then(|c| c.as_os_str().to_str())\n                                .map(|s| s.to_string())\n                        } else {\n                            None\n                        }\n                    });\n\n                Ok(vec![SessionInfo {\n                    session_id,\n                    start_offset: 0,\n                    end_offset: file_size,\n                    metadata: None,\n                    parent_session_id,\n                }])\n            }\n            _ => {\n                // For other detection methods, we'd need to parse the whole file\n                // For Phase 1, we only support one-file-per-session for JSONL\n                Ok(vec![])\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use
